item.title: Are AI-generated short dramas a waste of computing power?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Are AI-generated short dramas a waste of computing power? Editor's Note: Currently, China's economy is steadily advancing along the path of high-quality development, even as domestic and international circumstances become increasingly complex. Some Western media, due to misunderstanding or bias, have repeatedly questioned or even distorted China's economic development. Accordingly, the Global Times launches the "Q&A on China's Economy" column to publish opinion pieces to present facts and clarify perceptions. Recently, a set of figures on the share of token consumption by large artificial intelligence (AI) models has drawn considerable public attention in China. According to the figures, short dramas and video generation account for 55 percent of domestic token consumption, e-commerce and marketing 24 percent, and software development only 15 percent. Some have contrasted this with the claim that "58 percent of US tokens go to writing code and enterprise automation," giving rise to the catchy narrative that "China uses computing power to chase entertaining short dramas, while the US uses it to build the future." Set against the current international discourse surrounding China-US competition in AI, the comparison is certainly attention-grabbing. Yet it does not withstand even the most basic fact-checking or scrutiny. The claim that "AI short dramas and video generation account for 55 percent" originated from an industry assessment, which circulates online and is contained in the investor-relations records of a listed company that is itself heavily invested in AI-generated short dramas. It is not a comprehensive calculation based on any authoritative statistical framework. Doubao has also recently clarified that the computing-power figures are "somewhat unreliable" and that, at ByteDance itself, only about 10 percent of the company's total compute is used for training and inference of video-generation models. As for the claim that "58 percent of the US token go to writing code," no authoritative source for the figure can be found at all. Tokens are units used to measure and bill AI model usage, reflecting workload and computing consumption. They are neither a measure of productivity nor an equivalent of GDP, and therefore cannot be used directly to gauge the value of a country's AI industry. Meanwhile, video generation is a computationally intensive use case, while code generation is relatively low in token intensity but highly efficient. Comparing the two simply on the basis of token consumption is therefore methodologically unsound. What matters is not how many tokens are consumed, but what value they create. China has the world's most complete and largest industrial system, giving AI an exceptionally rich range of application scenarios and the world's largest real-world testing ground. Short dramas, e-commerce, livestreaming and content generation may not fit the conventional image of cutting-edge, "hard-core" technology. Yet it is precisely these everyday applications that place AI technology on the front line, where it is tested by real users and repeatedly refined through viable commercial cycles. A video-generation model used thousands or tens of thousands of times in short-drama production must meet real requirements for visual consistency, production deadlines and cost efficiency. This model has far more opportunities to be updated, iterated and improved - and can generate far greater industrial value-than a technology used only by a small number of engineers or one that exists largely in PowerPoint presentations. "Mass-market" does not mean "low-value," and mass adoption should not be set against frontier research. The scale of application itself helps fund research and points it toward the problems that matter. Large-scale use spreads inference costs across more users, helping transform model services from expensive laboratory tools into affordable public goods. In China, some video-generation models now cost less than one yuan per second, while AI short-drama production costs have fallen from several thousand yuan per minute to only a few hundred. Lower costs bring more small businesses and individual creators into the market, expanding the range of applications. In turn, the engineering challenges exposed by large-scale use help shape research priorities. China's strengths in open-source models, lightweight deployment and low-cost inference have, to a large extent, grown out of the demands of serving AI at scale. China's AI development is by no means focused only on applications at the expense of technological research. A 2024 report by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) already showed that China leads the world in the AI research publication volume, citations counts and patent output, and is world's largest source of generative AI patent publications. Chinese AI models have led weekly usage on OpenRouter, the world's largest AI model API aggregation platform, for 26 consecutive weeks, accounting for roughly two-thirds of total usage. The share of tokens used for coding tasks on the platform rose from about 10 percent in February to around 50 percent in September this year. China has never been absent from the development of foundational capabilities or frontier models. More importantly, it has not kept these advances locked inside laboratories. Instead, it has pursued development on two fronts, allowing research and development to interact with and reinforce the world's largest pool of real-world demand. There is little reason to fuel anxiety about "China falling behind the US in AI" with questionable data. Turning statistics based on inconsistent methods and unclear sources into a simplistic contrast between "building the future" and "chasing short dramas" risks misleading the public and politicizing normal technological diffusion and industrial specialization. Large-scale application is, in fact, one of the strongest foundations of China's AI development. By closing the loop between research and real-world deployment, China is pursuing its own path while also creating greater room for the global diffusion of AI technologies and their industrial applications. item.title: China firm advocate of, doer in reforming, improving global governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
China firm advocate of, doer in reforming, improving global governance On Oct. 23, Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a letter to the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an), further elaborating on the importance of reforming and improving the global governance system and charting the course for advancing the implementation of the Global Governance Initiative (GGI). The letter demonstrated China's sense of responsibility and its willingness to work with other countries to build a more just and equitable world. Xi put forward the GGI in September 2025, a much-needed initiative that offers solutions to bridge the governance deficit and build a better future. In just over a year, the initiative has gained the support of more than 160 countries and international organizations. Over 60 countries have joined the Group of Friends of Global Governance. Its core elements have been incorporated into the documents of multilateral fora such as the G20, the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, and BRICS. The past year has underscored the great contemporary value of the GGI, with its appeal and influence continuing to grow. The initiative has become an important public good warmly embraced by the international community. The international community regards the GGI as a stalwart for multilateralism as the international landscape is undergoing a profound shift, and a safeguard for fairness and justice as the law of the jungle makes a comeback. To many in the world, the GGI provides a clear pathway to shared development and security and much-needed certainty for a turbulent world. Beyond championing the GGI, China has taken decisive steps to translate its vision into practice. Since its launch, China has advanced multiple proposals to promote peace and stability in conflict zones such as the Middle East, voluntarily waived demands for additional special and differential treatment in World Trade Organization negotiations, and introduced new forms of international public goods, such as the International Organization for Mediation and the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. The GGI is widely regarded by people of foresight around the world as a remedy for and improvement on the existing international system, and a crystallization of Chinese wisdom that will shape a fairer, more inclusive, and more sustainable world. The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an), held in Xiong'an New Area in north China's Hebei province, marked a major step by China in working with other countries around the world to put the GGI into practice. Under the theme "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World," participants exchanged ideas and learned from one another. Their discussions addressed both the need to uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the governance of emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, cyberspace, and outer space. Through dialogue and communication, they sought to build consensus and develop joint solutions, contributing to international efforts to tackle governance challenges and reform and improve global governance. More than a policy dialogue, the forum offers the international community a tangible look at China's governance philosophy. In just nine years, Xiong'an New Area has transformed from a planned development zone into a dynamic innovation hub and a showcase of high-quality urban development. By engaging with this "city of the future," attendees witnessed firsthand how China's governance model -- centered on people-first development, ecological sustainability, technological innovation, and long-term planning -- has translated into measurable progress. This year marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations. As a founding member of the United Nations and a permanent member of its Security Council, China has consistently upheld and practiced multilateralism. At the forum, China announced eight practical actions to advance global governance. These include ensuring the success of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in November, continuing to engage deeply in United Nations reform and encouraging the Group of Friends of Global Governance to play a bigger role. The country called on all parties to uphold the central role of the United Nations, practice the values of fairness and justice, bolster the strength of the Global South for better global governance, advance in the direction of openness and development, and improve the rules of governance in emerging fields. These measures clearly demonstrate China's firm resolve to work with other countries to steer global governance toward greater fairness and equity. They also provide a roadmap for joint efforts to implement the GGI in the next stage. An African media outlet commented that the forum's significance lies in its efforts to foster a more open, balanced and constructive dialogue on the future of international relations. Global governance serves the common interests of all nations, and requires the collective effort of the international community. China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, build strength through confidence and overcome challenges through cooperation. Together, the international community can advance the implementation of the GGI, bring greater certainty and positive energy to a world fraught with change and turbulence, and work hand in hand toward a community with a shared future for humanity. item.title: China confirms identities of 8 more volunteer soldiers killed in Korean War
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
China confirms identities of 8 more volunteer soldiers killed in Korean War BEIJING, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- China has confirmed the identities of eight more Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) martyrs who lost their lives during the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea (1950-1953), the Ministry of Veterans Affairs said on Wednesday. This marks further progress in efforts to identify the remains of CPV martyrs repatriated from the Republic of Korea (ROK), the ministry said. More than 70 years ago, the CPV crossed the Yalu River and fought alongside the army and civilians of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) against the ROK army and U.S.-led UN forces. China sent 2.9 million CPV soldiers to assist the DPRK during the war, of whom more than 360,000 were killed or injured. Most of the fallen CPV soldiers were buried on the Korean Peninsula. According to an agreement between China and the ROK signed in late 2013, the two sides consult every year on the handover of remains of Chinese soldiers found in the ROK. Since 2014, China and the ROK have completed 13 consecutive handovers involving the remains of 1,023 CPV martyrs. In recent years, China has intensified efforts to identify the remains of CPV martyrs, including the creation of a DNA database for martyrs and their relatives, offering solid technical and data support to help more families find their missing loved ones. To date, the identities of 44 of the martyrs have been confirmed and their relatives have been located. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Upholding the United Nations' ideals and working together for humanity's future
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Upholding the United Nations' ideals and working together for humanity's future This year marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations (UN). Over more than half a century, China has steadily evolved from a participant in the international system into a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development, and a defender of the international order. This journey reflects not only a major country's growing engagement in global governance, but also how the spirit of the UN Charter has taken root in the modern world. On Oct. 25, 1971, the 26th session of the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758 by an overwhelming majority, deciding to restore all the rights of the People's Republic of China in the UN and recognizing the representatives of its government as the only legitimate representatives of China to the UN. In his article "Renewing Multilateralism: China and UN in the 21st Century," former UN Resident Coordinator in China Siddharth Chatterjee wrote that, 55 years on, this decision endures as a defining milestone in the evolution of the international order. Over the past 55 years, China has evolved from embracing international rules to contributing ideas for global governance. Throughout this journey, it has consistently supported the UN, upheld the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and played an active and constructive role within the UN framework. China has advanced the building of a community with a shared future for humanity and made significant contributions to world peace and development. Stephen Jackson, the UN Resident Coordinator in China, noted that China brings a distinctive perspective from the Global South to the UN, helping to create a more balanced global governance landscape. China has always been a builder of world peace. Guided by the Chinese nation's deep-rooted commitment to peace, China has chosen the path of peaceful development, rejecting the traditional route of aggression and expansion taken by major powers. Among the world's major countries, China has the best track record with respect to peace and security. China is the second-largest contributor to the UN peacekeeping budget and the largest provider of peacekeeping personnel among the permanent members of the UN Security Council. To date, it has dispatched more than 50,000 peacekeepers to 29 UN Security Council-authorized peacekeeping operations. As conflicts continue to flare around the world, China has worked to promote peace and dialogue. From the Russia-Ukraine conflict to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, it has pursued approaches to resolving hotspot issues with Chinese characteristics and played a constructive role in easing tensions and resolving disputes. China has consistently contributed to global development. It achieved the poverty reduction goals set under the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development 10 years ahead of schedule and contributes around 30 percent of global economic growth. It is now a major trading partner for more than 160 countries and regions and has signed 24 free trade agreements with 31 countries and regions. The country has signed Belt and Road cooperation documents with over 150 countries and 30 international organizations, injecting fresh momentum into global development. In response to widening global development gaps, China has actively worked to put development back at the center of the international agenda and help developing countries strengthen their capacity for self-sustaining growth, so that the benefits of development can be shared more widely and equitably among people in all countries. China has always upheld the international order. Over the past 55 years, it has firmly defended the UN-centered international system, the international order underpinned by international law, and the basic norms governing international relations, founded on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. China advocates and practices true multilateralism and actively leads and advances multilateral cooperation. It is a member of almost all universal intergovernmental organizations and a party to over 600 international conventions and their amendments. It has put forward Chinese solutions in emerging areas such as climate change and AI governance. China has successively proposed the four major global initiatives and taken the lead in implementing them, contributing Chinese wisdom and solutions to addressing deficits in peace, development, security and governance. The world is undergoing profound change and growing turbulence, while global challenges continue to mount. The international community must build consensus and work in concert to meet the challenges of our time. We should uphold fairness and justice, and strengthen the foundation of sovereign equality. The international community must firmly oppose hegemonic practices that allow the strong to bully the weak and must never let the world revert to the law of the jungle. International affairs should be discussed and decided by all countries together, and the legitimate concerns of developing countries must be heard and taken seriously. Only in this way can the foundations of the multilateral international order remain firm. We should uphold fundamental principles while breaking new ground to improve UN governance. Upholding fundamental principles means adhering to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, safeguarding the international system and the basic norms governing international relations established after the end of World War II, and remaining committed to multilateralism. Innovation means responding to the changing times by enabling the UN to adapt and reform itself, continually improving its internal governance mechanisms, enhancing its effectiveness and better reflecting the concerns of developing countries. We should shoulder our shared responsibilities and put multilateralism into practice. More than 190 countries in the world are all aboard the same big boat, bound by a shared destiny. Only by working together can they weather the storms ahead. All parties should embrace the principle of extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, explore new approaches to cooperation and develop innovative cooperation models, while continuing to advance multilateralism in response to changing global circumstances, and working together to address global challenges such as climate change, food security and digital governance. At this new historical juncture, China will continue to be a staunch supporter of the UN and a steadfast practitioner of multilateralism, working hand in hand with other countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity and create a better world for all. item.title: Xi extends condolences over death of Japan's former PM Yasuo Fukuda
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Xi extends condolences over death of Japan's former PM Yasuo Fukuda BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended condolences over the death of former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda to his family. In his message, Xi also extended sympathy to the family. Fukuda was a Japanese statesman known for his integrity and sense of responsibility, as well as a longtime friend of the Chinese people. He had long been committed to the China-Japan friendship and upheld a correct view of history, Xi said. During his tenure as prime minister, he signed the fourth political document between China and Japan with the Chinese side, setting out important principles for the development of bilateral relations, Xi said. Fukuda also served as chairman of the Boao Forum for Asia, playing an important role in promoting exchanges and cooperation in Asia, Xi said, noting that China will remember his contributions to China-Japan relations and Asia's development. Xi also expressed the hope that Fukuda's family would carry on his legacy and continue to work for China-Japan friendship. Xi expressed the hope that Japanese authorities would cherish the efforts of previous generations of statesmen, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and safeguard the political foundation of bilateral relations. item.title: Why the CPC puts people's well-being at the heart of self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Explainer: Why the CPC puts people's well-being at the heart of self-governance This photo taken on March 12, 2026 shows the Great Hall of the People ahead of the closing meeting of the fourth session of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) in Beijing, capital of China. (Xinhua/Li Yan) BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- In northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, eligible residents can receive certain forms of medical assistance and other support without submitting an application. Government departments share the information needed to provide the benefits. The provincial bodies responsible for disciplinary inspection helped drive the change. They prompted civil affairs departments to build a data-sharing network connecting 33 departments and institutions, enabling 12 frequently used assistance services to be provided without applications. The initiative offers a concrete example of how the self-supervision of the Communist Party of China (CPC) improve public services and help ensure that benefits reach those who most need them. Earning public trust through tangible improvements in people's lives is a defining feature of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance, which is high on the agenda of the fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee. The key meeting, which opened Monday in Beijing, is considering a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. COMMITMENT TO THE PEOPLE The CPC constitution commits the Party to serving the people, and states that it has no special interests of its own apart from those of the working class and the broadest possible majority of the people. Without seeking self-interest, the CPC can keep its spirit of thorough self-reform, and by swiftly detecting and resolving its own problems, the Party can prevent any interest group, power group or privileged stratum from preying on or corrupting its members. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels. Gyula Thurmer, president of the Hungarian Workers' Party, said serving the interests of the people is a central principle of the CPC. He added that the Party's anti-corruption efforts have achieved significant results, strengthening internal discipline and helping implement major economic and social development programs. Students build circuits during a science festival at a primary school in Wuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Sept. 29, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Xiaobang) SAFEGUARDING PEOPLE'S INTERESTS Xi has called on Party members to bear in mind that "benefiting the people is their greatest political achievement." An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan (11.5 billion U.S. dollars) in money and property to the public. Faruk Boric, president of the Association of Friendship between China and Bosnia and Herzegovina, said China's efforts to pursue corrupt officials at both senior and lower levels send "a clear message that no official is above the rules, regardless of their position." He said China's experience offers important lessons in linking clean governance with people's well-being. Protecting public funds, he added, helps direct more resources toward health care, education and other public services. Cao Fudi carries chili peppers for drying at Huangling scenic area in Wuyuan County, east China's Jiangxi Province, Sept. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang) BUILDING BETTER GOVERNANCE On several occasions, Xi has called for taking simultaneous, coordinated, and comprehensive steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to become corrupt. In his article on the Party's self-reform, Xi urged efforts to improve Party conduct, enforce discipline, and fight corruption, while integrating Party self-supervision with public oversight to deeply advance the Party's self-reform. Lyazid Benhami, a member of the Paris Association of French-Chinese Friendship, said rigorous Party self-governance can clarify officials' responsibilities, improve coordination and help sustain development programs. He highlighted China's emphasis on long-term planning, infrastructure, education and research, adding that the country has achieved a profound transformation regarding such priority areas and improved the well-being of its people. Those administrative strengths matter as China implements its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). In January, Xi urged efforts to confine power to an institutional cage in a more well-conceived and effective manner, and press ahead with the anti-corruption fight with a clearer understanding and stronger resolve, thus providing a strong guarantee for achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Volker Tschapke, honorary president of Germany's Prussian Society, said the CPC's courage to "turn the blade inward" demonstrated a "moral strength that I truly admire." He stressed that rigorous Party self-governance ultimately serves the fundamental interests of the people. "I have seen with my own eyes what that has achieved: how villages have blossomed through targeted poverty alleviation, how rural areas have found new hope, how high-speed rail connects people and hearts," he said. item.title: Xi congratulates Lula on re-election as Brazilian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
Xi congratulates Lula on re-election as Brazilian president BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended congratulations to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election as president of Brazil. In his congratulatory message, Xi said that President Lula has made important contributions to advancing China-Brazil relations. Xi said he and Lula have, in recent years, maintained close communication through various means and jointly guided the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future for a more just world and a more sustainable planet to new progress. The global, strategic and long-term significance of the bilateral relationship has become increasingly prominent, making it a model of solidarity and cooperation among Global South countries, he said. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brazil relations and stands ready to work with President Lula to guide the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future to new heights, open up broader prospects for all-round strategic coordination between the two countries, and continuously enhance the well-being of the two peoples. Also on Tuesday, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng sent a congratulatory message to Geraldo Alckmin on his re-election as Brazil's vice president. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
